answer.rationale: Competitor pricing pressure and rising SMB churn create urgency, but the archived experiment exp_73 (feeding memory_73) explicitly shows that targeted discounting drives short-term acquisition at the cost of a -12% 30-day retention and failure to survive renewal—an unsustainable trade against the stated objective of long-term qualified revenue. Referral incentives (memory_57/exp_57) are confirmed effective only for accounts older than 6 months, which may not match the price-sensitive SMB cohort now at risk, so scaling that lever broadly would be an unverified generalization. Enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) targets a different segment entirely. Given the verification budget is exhausted, the safest move consistent with existing evidence is a small, guarded activation-messaging test (memory_91) aimed at improving engagement and perceived value for the at-risk SMB base, which does not carry the known retention-collapse risk of discounting and can be scaled if it shows durable engagement lift. This avoids repeating a previously flagged failure mode while still responding to the immediate churn signal.
